article: Who pays when an agent works?

sources.title: 2025: The State of Generative AI in the Enterprise
sources.definition: Estimated enterprise generative AI spending. The 2025 report restates 2023 and 2024 to exclude inference. Scope excludes chips, inference/model serving, and AI features bundled into existing software.
sources.method: Market sizing combines public data, a bottom-up market model and a November 7–25, 2025 survey of 495 US enterprise AI decision-makers at companies already using AI. Private-company revenue estimates are uncertain.
sources.use: Chart 1; evidence of enterprise purchasing budgets, not agent wealth or operator funding prevalence.

sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Board; underlying data from US Census Bureau BTOS
sources.title: The AI Buildout and the Economy: Publicly Available Data to Assess AI’s Impact (Accessible Data)
sources.locator: Figure 8: AI Adoption Rates by Firm Size; row dated 6/14/2026
sources.definition: Four-period moving average of biweekly data on businesses reporting AI use in the last two weeks, by employment size. This is not a raw single-period observation.
sources.use: Chart 2; AI use exists among small businesses. Neither AI use nor employment size measures agent operation, owner wealth or credit access.

sources.title: Are Firms Financially Constrained?
sources.definition: Share of respondents reporting that access to financing or its cost constrained investment or spending plans.
sources.calculation: Not constrained = 100 minus the rounded published constrained share of 19 = 81. The 81 figure is not independently transcribed.
sources.use: Chart 3; financing constraints are not universal among surveyed human businesses. Not a population estimate for all businesses, distressed economies or agent operators.
